summary: This article explains where an oasis gets its water, how people farm and live around it, and why its water must be used with care.
introduce: Read the title “Oases: Water in the Desert” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: water that is stored under the ground, in soil and rock
a layer of rock or sand under the ground that holds water
a group of people and animals, such as camels, traveling together over a long distance

challengeTerms.def: to fill something up again after it has been used
to change from a liquid into a gas, often because of heat
able to continue for a long time without using up or harming resources

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that water under the ground will never run out? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain where an oasis gets its water and why people must use that water carefully.
struggling: Pre-teach groundwater, aquifer, and caravan with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses replenish, evaporate, and sustainable to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
